name: Point Look
description: A pointing hand and a pair of eyes—the gesture of directing someone's attention at something worth watching. Used to say 'look at this' or 'did you see that,' often with an undertone of significance or intrigue.
meaning: The pointing hand directs attention outward; the eyes emphasize the act of looking. Together they mean 'check this out' or 'look what I found,' with the implication that whatever is being pointed at is interesting enough to warrant a second glance.
examples: wait 👉👀 at what she just posted
seoDescription: What does 👉👀 mean? A pointed gesture to look at something specific—used to direct attention at a link, post, or moment worth noticing.

longForm.overview:
👉👀 is the combo that turns 'look' into 'look at THIS.' The pointing hand narrows the field of vision—it is not a vague 'look around,' but a specific 'look here'—while the eyes confirm the action of looking itself. The two emojis together create a sense of directed attention that feels more urgent than either one alone.

In practice, 👉👀 lands in conversations where someone has spotted something notable and wants to make sure you do not miss it. It can be straightforward ('i found a good deal 👉👀'), gossipy ('did you see what he tweeted 👉👀'), or pointed ('the hypocrisy 👉👀'). The combo works because the picture is self-explanatory—a hand pointing, eyes looking—and that clarity is what makes it so useful as a standalone reaction.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
👉👀 shows up most often when someone wants to draw attention to a link, a post, a behavior, or a moment without typing out a full sentence. It lands under TikToks as a 'this is the part you need to see,' under screenshots as 'look at this detail,' and in group chats as 'did you catch that.' The combo is faster than saying 'look at this' and carries a slight note of significance—the sender is essentially saying 'this matters enough to interrupt the conversation.'

On Twitter and Instagram, 👉👀 often precedes a reveal or marks something that deserves a second look. In Discord and Slack, it functions as a nudge to a specific message or thread. The combo rarely arrives alone in formal settings; it is almost always paired with context that explains what is being indicated.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 👉👀 when you are pointing out someone's mistake in a professional setting where tone matters. A manager sending 👉👀 at a coworker's error can read as condescending or mocking, even if the intent was neutral. In serious conversations—someone sharing bad news, a friend opening up—the combo feels too light and observational. It also does not work well as a solo reaction to something sad or sensitive; a heart or a simple 'i see you' lands better.

Do not use 👉👀 to direct attention at someone's appearance or body in a way that could feel invasive. The combo's directness can amplify an uncomfortable moment if the thing being pointed at is personal. When in doubt, lead with text that explains why something deserves a look, rather than relying on the emoji to carry that weight.
longForm.howToReply:
If you receive 👉👀 with a link or a screenshot, the appropriate reply is usually to click through and respond to the actual content. If the sender is pointing out something funny, you can mirror the energy with 😂 or your own 👉👀. If someone sends 👉👀 at your post and you want to acknowledge it, a simple thanks or 'right??' works—the emoji does the heavy lifting, so you do not need to match it.

If the combo lands on something you did not intend to highlight, a clarifying question is fair: 'what am i looking at' is a reasonable response if the reference is unclear. If you want to escalate the energy after receiving 👉👀 at something juicy, you can reply with 🍿 or 'spill,' inviting the sender to elaborate on what they spotted.

faqs.question: Is 👉👀 flirty?
faqs.answer: Not inherently. 👉👀 is neutral about tone—it is just directing attention at something. It can land in a flirty context ('👉👀 your new profile pic') but the flirtation comes from the surrounding message, not from the emoji combo itself.

faqs.question: What does 👉👀 mean in a group chat?
faqs.answer: Usually 'look at this thing I just saw or found.' It can be gossip, a funny post, a deal, or something someone said. The group chat context makes it feel more casual and less investigative than it might in a one-on-one conversation.

faqs.question: Can 👉👀 be mean?
faqs.answer: It can read as pointed if the thing being pointed at is someone's mistake or bad take, but the emoji itself is not mean—the meaning lives in what is being indicated. Sending 👉👀 at someone's own words can feel like 'look what you just said,' which lands as a callout.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 👉👀 and just sending 👀?
faqs.answer: 👀 alone means 'i am watching' or 'i am curious.' 👉👀 means 'look at THIS specific thing.' The pointing hand makes it directional and specific; the eyes make it about the act of looking.

conversationExamples.message: 👉👀 check the numbers in column D before you send this out
conversationExamples.interpretation: A coworker is flagging a specific detail that needs attention before a deliverable goes out. This is a helpful nudge, not a criticism. Reply by looking at what was flagged and confirming you caught the issue.

conversationExamples.message: wait 👉👀 the way they're acting around each other now
conversationExamples.interpretation: A friend is pointing out a shift in dynamics they noticed—possibly romantic tension or a friendship change. They want you to observe it too. An appropriate reply is to acknowledge you see it and speculate together.

conversationExamples.message: 👉👀 just saw this and thought of you
conversationExamples.interpretation: Someone is sharing a link, post, or observation because it reminded them of you in a positive way. It is a low-pressure way to show they were thinking of you. Reply with genuine interest in whatever was shared, or a simple 'aw thanks.'

conversationExamples.message: 👉👀 your brother's new car just pulled up
conversationExamples.interpretation: A family member is alerting you to something happening in real time—someone arrived, something changed, or there is something to see. This is usually a heads-up to pay attention to what is about to happen. You can acknowledge it or go look for yourself.

conversationExamples.message: 👉👀 the quote tweet replies are insane
conversationExamples.interpretation: Someone is directing your attention to a specific part of a viral moment—usually the commentary, drama, or absurdity that followed. They are saying 'you have to scroll the replies on this one.' It is an invitation to witness something entertaining or shocking.
